options.label: Immediate Rejection on Ground 1 (Licensing)
options.description: Reject Corvane's bid immediately based solely on the statutory bar of lacking the required C-16/C-20 license, avoiding any hearing or delay.

options.label: Strategic Partnership (Forced Subcontracting)
options.description: Condition the award on Corvane hiring Tasker & Moye as a subcontractor to perform the licensed work, thereby saving the low bid while fixing the license gap.

options.label: Cure Window for Reclassification
options.description: Treat the licensing error as a fixable responsibility issue rather than a statutory bar, granting Corvane 48 hours to hire a licensed subcontractor and cure the defect.

options.label: Full Hearing on All Grounds
options.description: Proceed with a vote on all three grounds (License, Addendum, Termination) and schedule a formal hearing to address the responsibility issues (Ground 3) to ensure due process.

options.label: Wait for Bidder Response
options.description: Delay the recommendation and vote to allow Corvane time to respond to the protest before the Board makes a final decision.

options.label: Immediate Rejection on Ground 1 (Licensing)
options.note: This is the most defensible path because Business & Professions Code § 7026.12 creates a statutory bar that renders a bid nonresponsive as a matter of law, allowing immediate rejection without a hearing and eliminating the risk of an award being set aside for illegal contracting.

options.label: Strategic Partnership (Forced Subcontracting)
options.note: This option is legally impermissible as it violates public bidding laws by altering the bid terms post-submission to favor a specific competitor, creating immediate exposure to a writ of mandate and potential bid-rigging allegations.

options.label: Cure Window for Reclassification
options.note: Granting a cure window for a statutory licensing violation is likely to be set aside as it treats a nonresponsive bid as a mere responsibility issue, undermining the integrity of the competitive bidding process and inviting litigation from other bidders.

options.label: Full Hearing on All Grounds
options.note: While this ensures due process for the responsibility claim, it unnecessarily delays the project schedule and creates exposure by subjecting the clear statutory licensing defect to a hearing that is legally unnecessary for nonresponsive bids.

options.label: Wait for Bidder Response
options.note: Delaying the decision to await a response to a facially nonresponsive bid based on a statutory bar is procedurally unsound, as the defect is incurable and the delay jeopardizes the project timeline without providing any legal benefit.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately distinguished between 'nonresponsiveness' (a fatal, incurable defect regarding the bid's face, such as the missing C-16/C-20 license) and 'responsibility' (a discretionary assessment of the bidder's fitness, such as the prior termination), advising that the statutory bar allows for immediate rejection without a hearing.
grade.overall: The optimal course is to immediately reject the bid based on the statutory licensing violation, as this is a nonresponsive defect that precludes award without a hearing and avoids the legal peril of attempting to cure a statutory bar. This approach best serves the client by adhering to the strict requirements of the Public Contract Code, protecting the district from litigation, and maintaining the project schedule.
